content.value_statement: Backend test suites often become slow, inconsistent, and hard to review. This skill gives Allra teams clear Java testing standards for choosing test types, data helpers, mocks, and assertions.
actual_capabilities: Recommends test helpers for integration, repository, controller, Redis, service, and POJO tests.
Explains when to prefer mocked unit tests over integration tests.
Provides JUnit 5, Spring Boot, Mockito, and AssertJ testing patterns.
Shows how to generate Java test data with Fixture Monkey.
Defines naming, display name, and Given-When-Then conventions.
Lists Gradle and Maven commands for running full or targeted tests.
limitations: It assumes the Allra Java and Spring Boot backend stack.
It does not create project-specific helper classes automatically.
Fixture Monkey and framework versions may need project review.
External service behavior still needs domain-specific mocking decisions.

use_cases.title: Choose a Test Type
use_cases.description: Decide whether a service change needs MockingUnitTest, IntegrationTest, RdbTest, ControllerTest, RedisTest, or PojoUnitTest.

use_cases.title: Standardize Test Reviews
use_cases.description: Check that new tests use clear names, Given-When-Then structure, AssertJ assertions, and focused verification.

use_cases.title: Improve Test Coverage
use_cases.description: Add missing tests for business rules, controller responses, repository queries, transactions, and data consistency.

prompt_templates.title: Pick the Right Test Helper
prompt_templates.prompt: I changed this backend class. Decide which Allra test helper I should use and explain the reason in simple steps.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Unit Test Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a MockingUnitTest plan for this service method. Include given, when, then, mocks, assertions, and edge cases.

prompt_templates.title: Review Existing Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these tests against Allra standards. Check helper choice, naming, Given-When-Then structure, assertions, and unnecessary integration coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Design Critical Workflow Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Design focused test coverage for this money or transaction workflow. Separate mocked unit tests from required integration tests.

output_examples.input: A service method validates input and saves one entity through a repository.
output: Use MockingUnitTest because the behavior is local to one service.
Mock the repository and verify the save call.
Assert the response fields and validation failure path.

output_examples.input: A payment workflow updates balances, creates payment records, and must roll back on failure.
output: Use IntegrationTest for the transaction boundary and database state.
Verify successful state changes and rollback behavior.

output_examples.input: A controller endpoint returns one user by id.
output: Use ControllerTest with the target controller slice.
Assert HTTP status, response fields, and validation errors.

best_practices: Start with MockingUnitTest unless transaction, database, event, or multi-service behavior requires integration coverage.
Use Given-When-Then sections so test setup, action, and verification stay clear.
Mock external APIs even inside integration tests unless the test explicitly covers that adapter.
anti_patterns: Do not use IntegrationTest for simple service validation or data mapping.
Do not assert only that a method returns without checking meaningful state or interactions.
Do not let Fixture Monkey generate unclear test data for fields that affect the expected result.

faq.question: Which test type should I choose first?
faq.answer: Start with MockingUnitTest for service logic. Move to IntegrationTest only when real transactions, constraints, or workflows matter.

faq.question: When is IntegrationTest required?
faq.answer: Use it for money flows, rollback behavior, multi-table consistency, database constraints, events, or required cooperation across services.

faq.question: Does this skill replace project test helpers?
faq.answer: No. It documents Allra testing standards and expected helper choices. Projects still need their own helper implementations.

faq.question: Can it help with Fixture Monkey?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows basic object generation, field overrides, and list generation for Java test data.

faq.question: Should external systems be real in integration tests?
faq.answer: Usually no. Mock payment gateways, notification services, and external APIs unless the adapter itself is under test.

faq.question: What naming style does it recommend?
faq.answer: It recommends method names that include the target method, scenario, and expected result, plus clear display names.
